Welcome to Source Material, a weekly series where the designers and creatives shaping culture share the references that shaped them. Our next guest is [Chase Rutherford](https://www.instagram.com/chase_rutherford/), the creative director for the YouTube duo [Slushy Noobz](https://www.youtube.com/@SlushyNoobz) (aka [Hamzah Al-Emad](https://www.instagram.com/hamzahthefantastic/) and [Martin Andrijasevic](https://www.instagram.com/thatmartinkid/)).

After the shoot, we caught up with Chase about his creative process:

**What’s the first thing you do when you sit down to work?**

Clean my room. It just really bothers me seeing trash and clothes on the floor. It feels like this when I don’t do it:

![A white dog squints beside flames in a meme captioned “he tryna ignore it,” followed by rows of loudly crying emojis.](data:image/png;base64,)![A white dog squints beside flames in a meme captioned “he tryna ignore it,” followed by rows of loudly crying emojis.](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/80762278364e4873924f0a322534a28a13957071-1290x1030.png?rect=1,0,1289,1030&w=528&h=422&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

**What’s a design object you’d take to your grave?**

Well, literally speaking, I just want to be cremated. Figuratively speaking, I would choose the [Yeezus CD](https://open.spotify.com/album/7D2NdGvBHIavgLhmcwhluK) because of its physical beauty and concept and also because it’s my favorite album ever and has deeply shaped who I am today.

**What current design trend are you tired of seeing?**

I appreciate all types of design because it’s a reflection of the collective. Without bad or distasteful design there’s nothing to react against.

Artist [Marcel Duchamp](https://www.moma.org/artists/1634-marcel-duchamp) coined the term [“readymade”](https://www.moma.org/collection/terms/readymade) in 1916 to describe ordinary, often mass-produced objects that are turned into art through small alterations or simply because the artist said so.

**What rule do you break the most?**

People don't really like when I do anything readymade. They think it's lazy or stealing, but what they don't see is me spending hours finding and recreating the exact fonts and graphics. But that's okay.

**What’s a piece of feedback you resisted, and later realized was right?**

I’ve been sitting here for five minutes, and I can’t think of anything. I’m kind of new to all this so maybe in a year I can come back to you and give you an answer.

**What’s a part of your process that most people don’t know about?**

I love love love to do the [Wim Hof breathing technique](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tybOi4hjZFQ&t=5s) after I run. It clears my brain in an indescribable way, being out of breath and lying on my floor, using my dirty clothes as a pillow, and knowing I have nowhere to be except on this floor for the next ten minutes. It’s so incredibly therapeutic and I recommend it to all my friends to try at least once.

**What’s the last thing you came across that made you want to go make something?**

This lady on my FYP eating the viral [“Crumbl Labubu ube dot cake Dubai chocolate matcha Korean chewy cookie”](https://www.tiktok.com/@moteaeats/video/7652182987504667918?_r=1&_t=ZP-9Am9f0JeVaw) inspired [my outfit](https://www.instagram.com/p/DeJ_8yPkZme/):
